title: Seven Nays, One Aye: The Solitary Burden of Command
summary: When all seven cabinet members voted 'No' and Lincoln voted 'Yes', the President calmly announced: 'Seven Nays, one Aye: The Ayes have it!'
keywords: Seven Nays, One Aye: The Solitary Burden of Command
full_text:
Under the United States Constitution, executive authority rests solely with the President; the Cabinet serves in an advisory capacity.

During a critical juncture of the Civil War, Lincoln convened his Cabinet to consider a vital executive measure. His secretaries—formidable statesmen like William H. Seward, Edwin Stanton, and Salmon P. Chase—vehemently opposed the proposal.

Lincoln called for a formal vote around the table:
"All those who oppose this measure, please signify by raising your hands."

Immediately, all seven cabinet members raised their hands:
"Nay!"
"Nay!"
"Nay!"

Every secretary looked triumphant, assuming the President was defeated.

Lincoln then asked with a smile:
"All those in favor, please signify by raising your hands."

Lincoln raised his solitary right hand: "Aye!"

The cabinet chuckled. Secretary Seward remarked: "Well, Mr. President, you are defeated seven to one!"

Lincoln struck the table with gentle finality and announced his ruling:

**"Seven Nays, one Aye: The Ayes have it!"**

Laughter erupted across the cabinet room, followed by sobering realization.

Lincoln explained with solemn sincerity:
"Gentlemen, I deeply value your counsel. But in the final audit of history, the responsibility for saving this Union rests not upon your shoulders, but upon mine alone!
When history judges this hour, it will judge Abraham Lincoln. Therefore, I must act according to my conscience!"

Recognizing his moral courage, the Cabinet closed ranks behind their Commander-in-Chief.
moral: A leader listens to all perspectives, but must possess the courage to shoulder solitary responsibility when conscience demands.
